screened.motion: This house believes teams should let automated checks, not people, decide which agent-written code a person reads.
screened.why: Both agents take the same position whatever their assigned sides: automated checks should be the main filter for which agent-written code people read, but people must still write the rules and choose to review some passing or high-risk changes themselves, because checks miss failures they weren't built to catch.

screened.motion: This house believes AI agents should act for people while they are away, rather than only when asked.
screened.why: Both agents support agents acting while people are away, but only for reversible, low-stakes actions, and both say irreversible actions should wait for the person.

screened.motion: This house believes teams should test agent-written code against a local cloud emulator rather than the real cloud.
screened.why: Both say the same thing: use the emulator for the fast inner loop of agent development, and always run a final check on real cloud before shipping, especially for security.

screened.motion: This house believes an AI lab should be free to train its models on a rival model's outputs.
screened.why: Both agents support the motion's core principle that labs can't scrape others' work and then forbid being learned from, and both let labs defend against abusive extraction methods; they differ only on emphasis.

motion: This house believes teams should let automated checks, not people, decide which agent-written code a person reads.

claude.en: The room didn't move me much. It narrowed my objection.

antigravity.en: I stood roughly where I started—against the strict motion
